title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy of Music on 1972-03-28
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of the March 28 1972 Academy run, featuring a smoking Brokedown Palace and a monster Playin' solo.
ai_review.review: The recording is a pristine SBD with superb separation that lets Keith’s organ and Pigpen’s harmonica shine, despite occasional minor distortion on Casey Jones and a tiny pitch‑correction issue. Musically the show is one of the strongest of the 1972 Academy stretch – tight first‑set cuts, a jaw‑dropping China Cat → Rider segue, an epic Playin' in the Dark solo, and a soaring Other One that caps a high‑energy second set.

ai_rating.rationale: All detailed reviews praise both the performance and the soundboard quality; only minor technical quibbles are noted, leading to an overall near‑perfect rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, well‑separated mix with excellent organ and harmonica presence; occasional Casey Jones distortion and a slight pitch‑correction on One More Saturday Night noted, but overall very listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A concise, high‑energy first set packed with classics that flow tightly into a second set of typical ’72 improvisations, highlighted by strong segues and an explosive jam climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Stellar steel guitar on Looks Like Rain, fiery solo in Playin' (building to a breaking point), tasteful wah on Sugar Magnolia coda.
band_member_comments.Phil: Provides tight harmony on Looks Like Rain; solid bass foundation throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Delivers a supernatural solo on China Cat Sunflower and drives the groove on Truckin'.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s organ is clear and often “supernatural” in solos, especially during the China Cat/Truck jam.
